ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
ux.task: Recover after the AI refuses to run because no provider is configured.
ux.finding: The one state that explains why AI does nothing tells the user to fix something they cannot fix. The panel says 'No API key is set for this workspace' and offers 'Open workspace settings'. There is no AI-key field on any settings screen in the product — the key is a server environment variable (OPENAI_API_KEY, or OLLAMA_BASE_URL for the local provider). The button lands the user on a 16-card settings index where nothing addresses the message they just read, and the message itself misnames the cause: it is a deployment fact, not a workspace setting. A workspace owner who follows the instruction has no way to discover that.
ux.evidence: AITab.tsx:261-277 renders the copy and the button (window.open(`${DASHBOARD_URL}/dashboard/settings`)). server/services/ai.service.ts:481-490 assertProviderConfigured reads process.env.OLLAMA_BASE_URL / process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY. `find packages/dashboard/app/dashboard/settings -name page.tsx` returns 16 pages (account, ai, api-tokens, billing, danger, domains, integrations, notifications, plans, profile, security, team, usage, workspace, root, vercel-team-picker); grep for 'OPENAI_API_KEY|apiKey|API key' across app/dashboard/settings and components/settings hits only integrations-tab.tsx:20 (Mailchimp). Searched: OPENAI_API_KEY, apiKey, 'API key', aiKey, provider.
ux.fix: Say what is actually true and give the state a real exit. For a workspace member: 'AI isn't available on this workspace yet' + a contact/support route. For an owner on a self-hosted deploy: name the environment variable. Never point at a settings page that cannot change the thing. If workspace-level keys are the intended future, build the field before the copy claims it exists.

ux.screen: History · version compare · 'Get AI Summary' + History · milestone suggestion banner
ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
ux.task: Read an AI summary of what changed between two versions; accept an AI-suggested milestone name.
ux.finding: Both History AI features very likely never reach the model. They post a bare JSON body to the tRPC HTTP endpoint, and that router is configured with the superjson transformer, which expects a {json, meta} envelope — a plain body deserialises to undefined and fails input validation before any handler runs. The user-visible result: 'Get AI Summary' shows 'AI summary unavailable' after a spinner, and the milestone banner simply never appears (its catch is silent). Neither test can catch it, because both stub fetch.
ux.evidence: useAISummary.ts:109-116 — `fetch('/api/trpc/ai.summarize', { method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({ versionName, changes }) })`, error path :132-140. useAutoMilestone.ts:180-198 — same shape for ai.milestoneSuggest, `catch { // Silently fail }`. server/trpc/trpc.ts:57 `transformer: superjson`. Every other AI call in the editor goes through a typed tRPC client that applies the transformer (subscriptionClient.ts, AiTrpcClient.ts:166-173) — these two are the only raw fetches. useAutoMilestone.test.ts:99 asserts only the URL and method against a stubbed fetch. Raises FIG-K-26 (recorded 'inferred') to a live UX defect. Also corrects D-F-38's claim that ai.summarize has no editor caller — it does, at useAISummary.ts:109; that row was already REFUTED in VERDICTS.jsonl:199 and is still being carried in DESIGN-AUDIT-SUMMARY.md:99. Searched: 'ai.summarize', 'ai.milestoneSuggest', '/api/trpc/', superjson, 'json:'.
ux.fix: Route both through the typed client the rest of the editor uses. Then give each a real failure state: the summary button needs a reason and a retry, and the milestone banner needs to stop being a feature the user can never discover is broken. Fix the tests too — a test that stubs fetch proves nothing about the transport.

ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.

ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.

The toggle reads 'Auto-apply steps (skip per-step approval)' — accurate about the mechanic, silent about the stakes — and the panel's own safety promise ('AI proposes a diff and never writes directly') is printed on the idle screen directly above the control that starts this run. Each approved step is its own transaction, so taking back a five-step auto-applied run is five separate undos with no single control that does it.

Server command vocabulary at server/services/ai.service.ts:685-745 includes delete-element, set-token, set-page-setting, save-as-component and propose-action; the client registry mirrors it at applySetStyle.ts:598-613. EmptyThread.tsx:56-58 prints the diff promise above the DRAFT row (AITab.tsx:344). ux.task: Get AI help on the surfaces where the work is hardest.
ux.finding: AI is absent from the three surfaces where it would earn the most and present on several where it earns least. There is no AI anywhere in Content/CMS — no field-schema suggestion, no 'write the body for these twelve records', no slug or excerpt generation — despite that being the most repetitive typing in the product. There is no AI in Insert or Layouts: a user cannot describe a section and get one, even though the server's add-section and insert-component commands exist. Meanwhile the version-history summary and the milestone-name suggester are both AI features on low-value, low-frequency surfaces, and both are broken (UX-G-09).
ux.evidence: CMS/Content: grep for ai|sparkle|generate|suggest across packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/content/ returns only page-generation copy ('Generates N pages from published records', ContentViews.tsx:632-672) — no AI affordance. Searched: 'ai', 'AI', Sparkles, 'Generate', 'suggest', '✨' in tabs/content — no hit. Insert: tabs/elements/constants.ts uses Sparkles as the 'Most Used' group icon only (:108). Server-side capability that exists but has no door: add-section and insert-component (server/services/ai.service.ts:704,739; applySetStyle.ts:606,608), ai.page and ai.layout (server/trpc/routers/ai.ts:183,208) reachable only through shared/utils/openai.ts:117-127 generateLayout, which is not exported and has zero callers. Image generation is typed but has no procedure at all (openai.ts:67-71 ImageRequest, AIPromptLibrary.ts:51 ImageStyle; no ai.image in the router). Searched: generateImage, ImageRequest, ai.image, generateLayout, ai.layout, ai.page.
ux.fix: Move AI to where the repetition is. Content/CMS records and fields first (bulk copy, slugs, excerpts, alt text at the record level), then a describe-a-section entry in Insert built on the add-section command that already exists. Take the version-summary and milestone-name features out rather than repairing them — they are AI applied to a job the user does once a week.

ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
ux.task: Continue working on a site that AI drafted.
ux.finding: The AI draft is handed to the editor and then forgotten. The onboarding wizard collects a full brief — industry, description, location, tone, visual style, colour, reference sites — generates a site, and drops the user into the editor with none of it. The editor does not know the site was AI-drafted, cannot show the brief, cannot regenerate a page against it, and the in-editor AI has no access to it either: every prompt starts from zero context about what this site is for. The 'Regenerate draft' button exists only on the onboarding preview screen, which the user can never return to.
ux.evidence: Brief captured: app/onboarding/ai/basics/page.tsx:37 and brand/page.tsx:33 write into wizard data; lib/onboarding/ai-input.ts buildGenerateInput consumes it. Handoff: app/onboarding/ai/preview/page.tsx:136-137 'Open in Editor' → openEditor(siteId); :149-152 'Regenerate draft' lives on that page only. Editor side: useComposerInit.ts:120-148 constructs the composer with remoteSync + aiClient and no brief; AITab.tsx:78-134 builds the scope from elements, tokens and media assets only (aiScopeContext.ts gatherTokens/gatherMediaAssets) — no site description, tone or audience. Searched: brief, industry, tone, wizardData, buildGenerateInput, aiScopeContext.
ux.fix: Persist the brief on the site and give the editor's AI read access to it, so 'make the hero warmer' is answered by something that knows the business is a restaurant in Lahore with a professional tone. Then put 'Regenerate this page' where a user can actually reach it — the Pages panel — rather than on a wizard screen they leave once.

ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
ux.task: Do the work anyway after AI refuses.
ux.finding: Both blocked states offer exactly one button, both leave the editor, and neither offers the obvious alternative: doing it by hand. 'See plans' opens billing in a new tab; 'Open workspace settings' opens a settings index (and cannot help — see UX-G-01). Neither state says what the user was trying to do, neither preserves the prompt they typed, and neither says 'you can still change this yourself in the inspector'. A user who hits the daily cap on their tenth edit is shown a pricing page and nothing else.
ux.evidence: AITab.tsx:249-277 not-configured (one Button, window.open to /dashboard/settings) and :278-296 quota (one Button, window.open to /dashboard/settings/billing). Both render INSTEAD of the thread (the ternary at :249 replaces ChatThread entirely), so the conversation and the typed prompt disappear behind the state. Only the third, unboarded 'other' state at :297-330 offers Try again with the remembered prompt (lastPromptRef, :76). Prior finding D-F-37 (findings/F.jsonl) recorded the same dead end from the board side. Searched: errorKind, 'not-configured', quota, lastPromptRef, DASHBOARD_URL.
ux.fix: Keep the thread and the prompt on screen behind the state — losing the user's typed words is a second failure on top of the first. Add the manual route as the second action on both states, and open billing in-place with a return, not a new tab that strands the editor session.

ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
ux.task: Find the AI assistant.
ux.finding: The cheat sheet teaches a shortcut for a panel that has no button. 'I — Open AI panel' is listed under Panels, and pressing I does open something — the left drawer variant of the AI panel — but there is no AI icon in the rail to connect it to, because the shipping rail deliberately omits AI. A user who learns the shortcut and then looks for the corresponding rail icon will not find one; a user who never opens the cheat sheet has only the inspector chips, which appear at the far right and read as element metadata rather than a tool.
ux.evidence: KeyboardShortcutsPanel.tsx:27-29 builds the Panels group from `GROUPED_TABS_CONFIG.filter(t => t.shortcut)`, which includes the 'ai' entry (tabsConfig.ts:87-97, shortcut 'I', zone 'creation'). tabsConfig.ts:349-351 RAIL_FIGMA lists only add, layers, pages, assets, content, design — 'ai' is absent, and rail/__tests__/tabsConfig.figma.test.ts:48 asserts it must not be there. ProInspector.tsx:368-370 records the intent: 'The rail omits ai deliberately … the 2026-08-05 Figma arc put this chip on every inspector header instead.' rail/__tests__/tabsConfig.ai.test.ts still asserts the tab is registered in the creation zone with shortcut I. Searched: RAIL_FIGMA, RAIL_FIGMA_IDS, GROUPED_TABS_CONFIG, PANEL_SHORTCUTS.
ux.fix: Decide where AI lives and make every index agree. If AI is an inspector-column tool, drop it from the panel-shortcut list and the ⌘K 'Open AI panel' navigation command, and teach the shortcut next to the chip instead. If it is a rail tool, put it in the rail.

ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
ux.task: Reach AI from the command palette.
ux.finding: The palette offers two different AI entries that land in two different places, and one of them is only reachable by failing. 'Open AI panel' sits in the Navigation group and opens the left drawer; '✨ Ask AI instead ›' appears only when a query matches nothing and opens the inspector column. Same feature, two rows, two destinations, and the better-labelled one is the one a user can only find by typing something that does not exist.
ux.evidence: CommandPalette.tsx:49-62 builds `Open ${tab.label} panel` for every tab with a shortcut and emits UI_PANEL_OPEN {panel: tab.id} — now allowlisted for 'ai' (useEditorEventListeners.ts:145-149), so it opens the LEFT drawer. CommandPalette.tsx:296-304 askAI emits ui:switch-tab {tab:'ai'} → the inspector column, and its own comment ('UI_PANEL_OPEN is allow-listed to real LEFT tabs and "ai" is not one — this offer has been a no-op since it shipped') is now stale. :463-470 renders the offer only inside the no-results branch (:440-471). Searched: askAI, UI_PANEL_OPEN, 'Ask AI instead', buildCommands.
ux.fix: One palette row for AI, always present, routing to the one AI home. Keep the no-results offer as a shortcut into that same row, not as a second destination.

ux.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
ux.task: Use one of the panel's own suggested prompts.
ux.finding: The panel's three starter prompts run against whatever scope happens to be active, and the panel does not warn when the suggestion and the scope disagree. 'Write alt text for every image' and 'Shorten the menu descriptions' are page-wide jobs; if an element is selected — which is exactly the state the inspector chip puts the user in, since the chip lives on the element header — the same click sends a single-element edit, and the user gets one change where the button promised many, with no message saying why.
ux.evidence: EmptyThread.tsx:26-30 TRY_PROMPTS; :44-53 each button calls onTry(p) → AITab.tsx:344 onTry={submit}. submit (AITab.tsx:78-134) branches on the CURRENT scope: element scope sends {kind:'element', id} and page scope sends the element list. useAIScope.ts:29-32 sets element scope on ELEMENT_SELECTED and seeds from the live selection at :49-60. The most common door into this panel — ProInspector.tsx:372-381 — is only rendered when an element IS selected. Searched: TRY_PROMPTS, onTry, toServerScope, useAIScope.
ux.fix: Suggestions should carry their own scope. A page-wide starter should set the scope to the page when clicked (and say so in the band), or be hidden when the scope cannot serve it. Silently narrowing a promise is worse than not offering it.

summary.purpose: AI experience — the cross-cutting layer where the editor offers to write, restyle, summarise or build something on the user's behalf.
summary.finding: PURPOSE — AI in Buildrick is meant to be the shortcut past the two slowest jobs in a website builder: writing copy and making a first draft look right. It is not a module; it is a layer that touches Canvas, Inspector, Brand, Media, Pages/SEO, History, Content and the dashboard's onboarding. PRIMARY TASKS — (1) draft a whole site from a business description (dashboard onboarding, real, wired to OpenAI, gated on OPENAI_API_KEY); (2) change the selected element or the page by describing the change (the AI panel and the canvas popover, real, wired through ai.streamPrompt with a proper propose→diff→apply→undo contract — this is the strongest AI surface in the product); (3) fill one field on request (SEO title, alt text — real but silent on failure and duplicated); (4) generate a design-system component (built, gated off by a flag nobody sets, and with no destination for its output); (5) summarise a version diff and name a milestone (built, almost certainly broken at the transport). ENTRY POINTS — fourteen, sharing five glyph vocabularies and four interaction shapes; the panel alone has six doors landing in two different columns. EXIT POINTS — '‹ Inspector', a close X, Escape from the popover, Discard on a diff, and two blocked states whose only buttons leave the editor. HANDS OFF TO — Canvas and Inspector (every applied edit), History (every edit lands as an 'ai-edit' transaction), Brand (tokens and component schemas), Media (alt text), Pages (SEO fields), Publish (the propose→confirm action gate), and the dashboard (billing, credits, generation jobs). RECEIVES FROM — element selection (scope), the token registry and media library (recall context), the plan/quota service, and the onboarding brief (which it is given at generation time and then never sees again). THE ONE SENTENCE — the engine underneath is better than the experience on top of it: a careful, well-designed diff-and-apply contract exists, and around it sit fourteen unlike buttons, three silent failures, two dead ends, two duplicated features, and a settings page that tells the user their AI features have not been built.
summary.evidence: Whole-lane census: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/ai/* (14 files), editor/canvas/controls/AiPromptPopover.tsx, editor/design-system/ui/AIPromptModal.tsx, editor/panels/version-history/{AIPanel.tsx,useAISummary.ts}, shared/hooks/useAutoMilestone.ts, services/ai/* (7 files), shared/utils/openai.ts, engine/designSystem/services/{AIAssistService.ts,ComponentSchemaAIClient.ts,aiErrors.ts}; server/trpc/routers/ai.ts (9 procedures), server/services/{ai.service.ts,ai-generation.service.ts,ai-actions.service.ts,ai-adoption.service.ts,alt-text.service.ts,openai.client.ts,ollama.client.ts}; packages/dashboard/app/onboarding/ai/*, app/dashboard/sites/new, app/dashboard/settings/ai, components/ai-wizard/*, components/settings/ai-credits-tab.tsx, app/api/workers/ai-generate. Flags: runtimeEnv.ts:87-88 FEATURE_DS_AI is the only AI flag and is set nowhere; there is no flag on the AI panel, the canvas popover, or any inline generate button — those ship to every user. Searched throughout: ai, AI, generate, suggest, assistant, prompt, wizard, OPENAI, OLLAMA, Sparkles, '✨', '✦'.
summary.fix: Adopt one AI interaction system before redrawing any of these screens — see docs/design-jobs/AI-PLACEMENT-MAP.md for the proposed placement rule, button hierarchy, and apply/cancel/retry/revert contract.
